correctness.rationale: Generic central cube sections have a bijection between section vertices and interior-intersected cube edges. Conditional on the normal coordinate Z_i, each of the \(2^{n-1}\) crossing indicators is a symmetric Gaussian-window indicator. Orthogonal even-Hermite expansion bounds pair covariance by squared Gaussian correlation times its mean. The exact average of these squared correlations is \(1/(n-1)\); conditional variance is therefore \(\le p/(n-1)\). Direct Gaussian integration gives a bias \(\le\sqrt{2/\pi}|Z_i|^3/[6(n-1)]\), and \(\mathbb E|Z_i|^6=15\). Cauchy angular probability gives \(\mathbb E p=(2/\pi)\arctan(1/\sqrt{n-1})\), yielding the stated mean-square error bound for every \(n\ge2\) and thus the fixed-r joint \(L^2\) limit. Moment convergence gives positive limiting variance and vanishing cross-covariance. The attached verifier replayed successfully on actual file bytes; it checks finite special cases only, not the infinite theorem. Risks: inaccurate classification of non-generic sections is excluded as measure zero; the Hermite identity includes \(\rho=\pm1\) by \(L^2\) continuity.

value.rationale: Cube hyperplane slices are canonical objects of convex and discrete geometry; direction-resolved section-vertex counts are intrinsic under labelled cube axes. This theorem determines a nondegenerate exact limit law for each direction and the full joint law for finitely many directions, beyond the classical expected total vertex count. It resolves a natural question about whether exponentially many dependent cube-edge crossing events self-average: instead each direction retains the absolute value of one Gaussian normal coordinate. The explicit all-n \(L^2\) bound and independence of the limiting fixed-coordinate vector are structural and reusable. Limitations: it does not answer growing-r behavior or the full total vertex-count distribution; no unrestricted face-vector theorem or paper-scale contribution is asserted.
